# Euclidean reduction and accumulated errors {#sec-tracking}

There are two different perturbations: an error caused by replacing the Stiefel retraction by its first-order Euclidean expansion, and the dependence of successive Monte Carlo observations.  Treating them separately makes the proof shorter and more transparent.

## A global second-order retraction estimate

::: {#lem-retraction}
## Polar retraction bounds

For every horizontal tangent vector \(U\) at \(W\in\mathrm{St}(d,r)\), constants \(c_r,c'_r<\infty\), depending only on \(r\), satisfy

$$
\|R_W(U)-W-U\|_F\leq c_r\|U\|_F^2,\qquad
\|R_W(U)-W\|_F\leq c'_r\|U\|_F.
$$ {#eq-retraction-bounds}
:::

::: {.proof}
Since \(W^\top U=0\), we have \((W+U)^\top(W+U)=I_r+U^\top U\), so

$$
R_W(U)-W-U=(W+U)[(I_r+U^\top U)^{-1/2}-I_r].
$$

When \(\|U\|_F\leq1\), the scalar inequality \(0\leq1-(1+t)^{-1/2}\leq t/2\), applied to the eigenvalues of \(U^\top U\), yields
\(\|(I_r+U^\top U)^{-1/2}-I_r\|_F\leq\|U\|_F^2/2\).
Also \(\|W+U\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\sqrt2\).  Thus the quadratic bound holds uniformly for small increments.  For \(\|U\|_F>1\), the triangle inequality and \(\|R_W(U)\|_F=\|W\|_F=\sqrt r\) give

$$
\|R_W(U)-W-U\|_F
\leq2\sqrt r+\|U\|_F
\leq(2\sqrt r+1)\|U\|_F^2.
$$

The linear estimate follows for small \(U\) from the quadratic one, and for large \(U\) from \(\|R_W(U)-W\|_F\leq2\sqrt r\).  This explicit global bound is convenient with unbounded MCMC observations; the local Taylor principle is described in @boumal2023, Section 4.1.
:::

Writing \(G_n=G(\mu_n,W_n,X_{n+1})\), @eq-coupled-algorithm becomes

$$
W_{n+1}=W_n+\gamma_{n+1}G_n+r_{n+1},
\qquad
\|r_{n+1}\|_F
\leq c_r\gamma_{n+1}^2\|G_n\|_F^2.
$$ {#eq-retraction-remainder}

::: {#lem-retraction-summability}
## Retraction errors are summable on eventually compact trajectories

Under @asm-kernel, @asm-step-sizes and @lem-observable-regularity, on the event that \((\mu_n,\Gamma_n)\) eventually stays in some compact subset of \(\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_{++}^d\),

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty\|r_{n+1}\|_F<\infty
\quad\text{almost surely}.
$$ {#eq-retraction-series}
:::

::: {.proof}
For a recursion stopped at its first exit from a compact \(K\), @eq-retraction-remainder and @eq-polynomial-regularity give
\(\|r_{n+1}\|_F\leq C_K\gamma_{n+1}^2V^{2\beta}(X_{n+1})\).  As \(2\beta\leq1\), the localized moment bound @eq-localized-moments makes the expectation of the nonnegative series at most \(C_K\sum_n\gamma_{n+1}^2\), which is finite.  Exhaust the open mean--covariance domain by countably many compacts; an eventually confined trajectory lies in a stopped regime after a finite prefix.
:::

## Decompose the controlled Markov fluctuation

The ambient recursion is

$$
\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n+\gamma_{n+1}
[h(\theta_n)+\xi_{n+1}]+(0,0,r_{n+1}),
\quad
\xi_{n+1}=H(\theta_n,X_{n+1})-h(\theta_n).
$$ {#eq-euclidean-recursion}

Let \(u_\theta\) solve @eq-poisson, and write \(v_\theta=P_\theta u_\theta\).  For \(k\geq1\), define

$$
M_k=u_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_k)-v_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_{k-1}).
$$ {#eq-martingale-difference}

Because \(X_k\) is conditionally distributed according to \(P_{\theta_{k-1}}\), we have
\(\mathbb E[M_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}]=0\).  Subtracting this quantity from the Poisson identity gives

$$
\xi_k=M_k+v_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_{k-1})-v_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_k).
$$

Multiplying by the step sizes and summing by parts, for \(m\geq n\geq1\),

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k=n}^{m}\gamma_k\xi_k
={}&\sum_{k=n}^{m}\gamma_k M_k\\
&+\gamma_n v_{\theta_{n-1}}(X_{n-1})
  -\gamma_m v_{\theta_{m-1}}(X_m)\\
&+\sum_{k=n}^{m-1}(\gamma_{k+1}-\gamma_k)v_{\theta_k}(X_k)\\
&+\sum_{k=n}^{m-1}\gamma_k
  [v_{\theta_k}(X_k)-v_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_k)].
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-weighted-poisson}

The decomposition has four conceptually distinct pieces: a martingale, two endpoints, step-size variation, and **accumulated differences of Poisson solutions**.  In particular, it is not a theorem about arbitrary retraction errors: those were already controlled in @lem-retraction-summability.

::: {#lem-noise-accumulation}
## Weighted noise has vanishing tails

Under the assumptions of @sec-assumptions, on eventually compact parameter trajectories,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{m\geq n}
\left\|\sum_{k=n}^{m}\gamma_k
[H(\theta_{k-1},X_k)-h(\theta_{k-1})]\right\|
=0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
$$ {#eq-noise-tail}
:::

::: {.proof}
The estimates are detailed in @sec-appendix-poisson.  In summary, the first line of @eq-weighted-poisson converges by the martingale \(L^2\) theorem and \(\sum\gamma_k^2<\infty\).  Its endpoints vanish by Borel--Cantelli.  The third line has absolutely summable coefficients because \(\gamma_k\) is nonincreasing.  For the final line, combine Poisson Lipschitz regularity with the parameter increment estimate

$$
\|\theta_k-\theta_{k-1}\|
\leq C_K\gamma_k V^\beta(X_k),
$$ {#eq-increment-estimate}

which follows from @lem-retraction and the first two Euclidean recursions.  Hence the last line is bounded in absolute value by \(C_K\sum_k\gamma_k^2V^{2\beta}(X_k)\), finite almost surely on the localized event.
:::

## ODE tracking, without a manifold-noise theorem

Set \(t_n=\sum_{k=1}^n\gamma_k\), and linearly interpolate the ambient coordinates between \(t_n\) and \(t_{n+1}\).  For any fixed \(T>0\),

$$
\sup_{\substack{m\geq n\\t_m-t_n\leq T}}
\left\|\sum_{k=n}^{m-1}
[\gamma_{k+1}\xi_{k+1}+(0,0,r_{k+1})]\right\|\to0.
$$ {#eq-ode-window}

The averaged field is locally Lipschitz; its Euler error on a compact set is \(O(\sum\gamma_k^2)\).  Comparing the interpolation with the integral equation for @eq-coupled-ode and applying Grönwall's inequality proves that the interpolation is an **asymptotic pseudotrajectory** of the ODE.  Its values between consecutive Stiefel iterates need not lie on the manifold; their distance to the manifold vanishes because @eq-increment-estimate and the weighted moment bound imply the step increment tends to zero.  The limiting flow itself preserves Stiefel orthogonality.

This is the usual Euclidean stochastic approximation method [@benaim1999], with the extra geometric term shown explicitly.
